claims.text: The Co-free alloy has an equiatomic Fe-Ni-Cr-Mn composition derived from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi by removing Co.
The initial Co-free alloy is a single-phase solid solution.
The initial Co-free alloy is in a recrystallized state.
The dynamic behavior of FeNiCrMn is governed by a temperature- and strain-rate-driven shift in the dominant dislocation mechanism.
Changes in stacking-fault energy with testing conditions modulate cross-slip and dynamic recovery.
At lower temperatures and higher strain rates, cross-slip is limited.
Limited cross-slip causes greater dislocation accumulation or pile-up and increased work hardening.
The low-temperature or high-strain-rate dislocation structure produces higher strength and lower ductility.
At higher temperatures or lower strain rates, cross-slip and dynamic recovery are enhanced.
Enhanced cross-slip and dynamic recovery reduce dislocation pile-ups and make plastic deformation more uniform.
The high-temperature or low-strain-rate dislocation structure improves ductility while moderately reducing strength.
Relative to CoCrFeMnNi, FeNiCrMn will have higher yield strength and lower ductility at lower temperatures or higher strain rates.
Relative to CoCrFeMnNi, FeNiCrMn will transition to lower strength and higher ductility at elevated temperatures or reduced strain rates.
TEM after higher-temperature deformation will show increased cross-slip and a more recovered dislocation structure.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi has a slightly higher stacking-fault energy than the Co-free alloy because it contains Co.
The slightly higher stacking-fault energy of CoCrFeMnNi makes its dislocation behavior less sensitive to temperature and strain rate.
The proposed mechanism applies from cryogenic to moderate temperatures and at strain rates where shifts in dislocation substructure remain observable.
Outside the stated regime, phase transformations or diffusion-controlled mechanisms may dominate the response.
